newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch to start tap sales of state bond on May 27.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to start tap sales of state bond on May 27.

text.p: The Dutch Finance Ministry said on Thursday it would start tap sales of a state bond on May 27 because of a market holiday in London the previous day.
The ministry earlier said it would announce details on May 23 of the only state bond issue planned for the second quarter of 1997, with sales to begin on May 26.
But a ministry spokesman told Reuters that May 26 was a market holiday (Spring Bank Holiday) in London, where many key corporate players in the Dutch bond market are based.
The key German Bund futures contract also trades on the London International Financial Futures Exchange.
"That's the main reason we will start selling on the 27th. Otherwise, (market players) will have difficulties matching with the futures contract," he told Reuters.
Most guilder bond players use the Bund futures to hedge their positions as the only Dutch futures contract is so illiquid.
Some dealers and traders will miss the start of tap sales as the International Securities Market Association (ISMA) is holding a conference in Singapore on May 28-30.
